paper.title: Beyond Meta-Reasoning: Metacognitive Consolidation for Self-Improving LLM Reasoning
paper.central_claim: MC2 (Meta-Reasoning Orchestrator inner loop + MetaCognitive Accumulator outer loop) consolidates structured Reasoner/Monitor/Controller traces across a stream into hierarchical meta-knowledge that is compiled into role prompts, yielding best accuracy across four benchmarks and four backbones with gains that grow as experience accumulates.

rationale: 冻结模型+跨实例分层元知识巩固，消融链含去记忆对照。但适应流即评测流、反思含正确性标签与'无真值'表述矛盾、经验曲线重复过题、无标签型记忆基线。

evidence.quote: most existing meta-reasoning methods remain episodic: they focus on executing complex meta-reasoning routines within individual instances, but ignore the accumulation of reusable meta-reasoning skills across instances
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: meta-reasoning methods do not carry skill across instances.

evidence.quote: we introduce Metacognitive Consolidation, a novel framework in which a model consolidates metacognitive experience from past reasoning episodes into reusable knowledge that improves future meta-reasoning.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: consolidated meta-level experience improves later meta-reasoning on the stream.

evidence.quote: These approaches primarily store task-level reasoning content (solutions, templates, or heuristics for solving), whereas we consolidate meta-level experience, how to monitor, critique, and control reasoning, into procedural meta-knowledge that progressively improves future meta-reasoning.
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed delta from ReasoningBank/Reflexion/Buffer of Thoughts/ReasonFlux; neither ReasoningBank nor Reflexion is run as a baseline, and the stored content (Table 10) mixes verification habits with domain tactics.

evidence.quote: We use a simple heuristic that leverages the MRO outcomes without requiring gold labels:
evidence.support_explanation: S+ = first-try Accept, S- = budget-exhausted Restart select reflections for distillation (Eq. 9).

evidence.quote: It is derived only from trace-visible fields (plus the correctness label) and does not require additional model calls.
evidence.support_explanation: The instance reflection includes a correctness-derived task_outcome tag; so ground-truth correctness (not the answer text) enters the consolidated memory.

evidence.quote: We use the correctness flag only as a binary outcome tag for reflection labeling
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms label use; conflicts with the label-free framing in Sec 4.2 (next item).

evidence.quote: enabling performance gains even without access to ground-truth supervision
evidence.support_explanation: Authors claim gains without ground-truth supervision, but no no-label variant is run.

evidence.quote: If regeneration still fails, we fall back to using the previous prompt
evidence.support_explanation: Only safeguard on LLM-composed role prompts is format/length validity with fallback to the previous prompt; no utility check or rollback on measured effect.

evidence.quote: batches are provided, so outdated rules are implicitly deprioritized without requiring explicit timestamps.
evidence.support_explanation: Forgetting is by sliding window (w=3, k=3 retrieval); consolidation is an LLM rewrite with no per-entry provenance or version.

evidence.quote: merging redundant lessons, resolving minor inconsistencies, and rewriting the remaining rules into a concise, role-executable form
evidence.support_explanation: Conflict handling delegated to the LLM consolidator; not evaluated.

evidence.quote: achieves the best accuracy across all backbone & benchmark combinations, demonstrating that metacognitive consolidation generalizes well across tasks and models.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 (3-run means, 95% CI): e.g. GPT-4o-mini MATH-500 85.13 vs best baseline 78.93, TheoremQA 55.96 vs 46.92, Game-of-24 88.67 vs 41.33; Qwen3-8B MATH-500 93.07+/-1.60 vs 91.93+/-1.52; Llama-3.1-8B Game-of-24 45.33+/-5.74 vs 41.00+/-8.96 (overlapping CIs).

evidence.quote: we run each method three times with different random seeds and report the mean performance along with 95% confidence intervals
evidence.support_explanation: Three seeds with CIs for Table 1; not for Tables 2, 6, 8, 9.

evidence.quote: we follow a best-effort reproduction strategy
evidence.support_explanation: All baselines re-implemented (no Python interpreter for Meta-Prompting; generic self-evaluation for ToT; TTPI uses perplexity only on GPT-4o-mini).

evidence.quote: Due to API constraints, we do not evaluate TTPI on Gemini-2.0-flash (no per-token log probabilities).
evidence.support_explanation: Missing baseline cells; baseline set contains no label-using, cross-instance memory comparator except Buffer of Thoughts (label-free).

evidence.quote: for multiple passes, and record accuracy and action statistics across both batches and iterations
evidence.support_explanation: Figure 1 / Fig 3 trend (about 84% at iteration 1 to 88% at iteration 5; severe restarts 33.1%->30.8%) comes from repeated passes over the same MATH-500 data on GPT-4o-mini with accumulated knowledge, so later passes can reuse lessons from the same questions.

evidence.quote: already delivers clear gains on both backbones and both datasets, showing that prompt-level meta-knowledge updates alone provide useful guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2 (GPT-4o-mini MATH-500/TheoremQA): Only Reasoner 72.67/44.04; Reasoner+Updates 80.47/50.46; R+M+C 79.20/47.38; +Micro-update 82.80/51.75; Full 85.13/55.96; Qwen3-8B 84.40/54.33; 90.80/59.79; 91.33/59.62; 92.60/62.21; 93.07/64.88. 'Updates' variant is not defined in the text; no CIs.

evidence.quote: Overall, these results provide preliminary evidence of cross-task transferability, while also confirming that the strongest and most reliable gains currently come from within-task consolidation.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 9 warm-start: GSM8K->MATH-500 83.60 vs 85.13 within-task; GSM8K->TheoremQA 57.00 vs 55.96; MATH-500->GSM8K 96.36 vs 96.92; MATH-500->TheoremQA 54.63 vs 55.96; single numbers.

evidence.quote: metacognitive knowledge by repeatedly processing instances drawn from the same benchmark or task distribution
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' scope: within-task consolidation on the evaluation distribution, not task-agnostic.

evidence.quote: Overall, we observe that shuffling the dataset order has negligible impact on final performance
evidence.support_explanation: Table 8: shuffled vs default, deltas -0.07/-1.34/+0.20/-0.66 on MATH-500 and Game-of-24 for two API backbones.

evidence.quote: we use GPT-5 as a binary judge to evaluate whether the updated role policies contains task-specific key operations/checkpoints that would materially help solve the given question
evidence.support_explanation: Table 7: p_keyops 0.9146/0.9618/0.9848 for Reasoner/Monitor/Controller; relevance of guidance judged by an LLM, no outcome link or control.

evidence.quote: incurs higher token usage than one-pass baselines, it is more efficient than compute-heavy test-time scaling methods
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 reports decoding tokens per instance for every method (e.g., GPT-4o-mini GSM8K MC2 833 vs CoT 358 vs CoT-SC 1805). Whether the distillation, consolidation and prompt-composer calls are included in #Tokens is not stated.

evidence.quote: enabling metacognitive consolidation incurs additional inference overhead, as the framework introduces multiple reasoning roles and periodic consolidation steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Author acknowledgement of overhead beyond one-pass methods.

evidence.quote: we conduct one full evaluation and report accuracy
evidence.support_explanation: Table 6 iteration-budget sensitivity is a single run: 84.6/85.8/83.2/82.4/84.4 for max iterations 2-6, i.e. non-monotone variation of about 3 points.

evidence.quote: For each dataset, the batch size is set to one-tenth of the dataset size, with a lower bound of 10 and an upper bound of 100.
evidence.support_explanation: Single pass in 10-14 batches; batch 1 is cold start; Game-of-24 has 100 problems (10 per batch).

evidence.quote: ReasoningBank Ouyang et al. (2025) and Reflexion Shinn et al. (2023) store experience from previous rollouts (e.g., trajectories and reflections) to guide future behavior.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest label-using experience-memory neighbours are cited but not compared.

evidence.quote: We find that first-try success is strongly aligned with correctness
evidence.support_explanation: Table 4 / Spearman rho=0.44: first-try Grade A has about 95.95% accuracy vs Grade C 38.82% (pooled over two backbones); supports the S+/S- heuristic as a noisy but informative proxy.

signatures.object: role policy prompts (Reasoner/Monitor/Controller) plus per-role meta-knowledge K_b and micro-lesson buffer; baseline fixed role prompts
signatures.information: MRO traces (answers, monitor error flags/locations, controller actions), deterministic reflections with correctness-derived task_outcome tag (gold answer text withheld), embeddings of question and lessons
signatures.operation: per batch: select S+ (first-try Accept) and S- (budget-exhausted Restart) reflections -> LLM distills role-specific micro-lessons -> LLM consolidates last w=3 batches into K_b -> retrieve top-3 lessons per instance -> LLM composer rewrites role prompts for next batch
signatures.output: updated role prompts used for the next batch's MRO inner loop
signatures.conditions: stream of same-task instances; batch size min(100,max(10,N/10)); batch 1 cold start
signatures.feedback: MRO outcome heuristics and correctness tag from the evaluation stream
signatures.selection_rule_data: heuristic S+/S- filter; composer output kept if parseable/within length else previous prompt; sliding window forgetting; no measured utility gate
signatures.persistence: K_b and micro-lessons in a buffer across batches (and across passes in the time-evolvement study)
signatures.claimed_effect: best accuracy on 16 benchmark x backbone cells; accuracy rises across passes; ablation ladder (Table 2)
signatures.failure_boundary: task-specific, same-distribution; label-dependent; overhead; LLM consolidation quality; order-insensitivity checked on two datasets

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the evaluation stream with correctness-tagged feedback, prompt-level consolidation of Reasoner/Monitor/Controller experience raised later-batch accuracy over fixed-prompt and label-free baselines, with a store-off style ablation showing +6 to +8 points on MATH-500/TheoremQA for the updates alone.
assessment.author_claim_vs_supported: 'Consistent gains that grow with experience' is supported only on-stream and partly via repeated passes; 'without ground-truth supervision' and meta-level specificity are not supported; transfer is preliminary.
assessment.note: retained is scoped to within-task online use of earlier items in the same stream; improver-level evidence absent (consolidator fixed).

G.reason: Real, specific gap (episodic meta-reasoning without cross-instance carryover) and a clearly changed object (role policy prompts and meta-knowledge), with neighbours named. Not 3-4: closest experience-memory neighbours (Reflexion, ReasoningBank) are not compared, the claimed meta-level vs task-level distinction is not tested and Table 10 shows domain tactics as well as verification habits.

M.reason: Reasoner-Monitor-Controller factorisation yields attributable action-critique-correction traces; reflections -> batch micro-lessons (successes and failures) -> windowed global rules -> retrieved lessons compiled into role prompts is a reconstructable chain with testable predictions (accuracy rises across batches, restarts fall, hierarchy > flat). Weaknesses: key framing 'no ground-truth' conflicts with label use, benefit of meta vs task-level content untested, LLM rewrite quality unchecked.

X.reason: Operation chain, batch size rule, w=3/k=3, embedding model, trace schema, deterministic reflection heuristics, composer validity checks with fallback, and window-based forgetting are specified. Gaps: no measured utility gate or rollback on effect, conflict resolution left to an LLM consolidator, 'Reasoner + Updates' variant undefined, stream/reset conventions across passes unclear, and prompt templates (App I) are not visible in the pinned HTML.

E.measurement.reason: Standard accuracy metrics on four benchmarks with a unified answer-parsing protocol, three seeds and CIs, token counts for all methods. Deductions: all baselines re-implemented best-effort (TTPI missing for Gemini, Meta-Prompting without interpreter), and correctness feedback is part of the method but not available to most baselines.

E.causality.reason: Ablation ladder (Only Reasoner / +Updates / R+M+C / +Micro / Full) includes a store-off style comparison and shows consolidation matters. Missing: label-free variant to test the stated claim, static optimised-prompt or shuffled-lesson control, comparison against label-using memory baselines (Reflexion/ReasoningBank) at matched calls, S+/S- heuristic ablation, and the headline 'grows with experience' curve uses repeated passes over the same questions.

E.holdout.reason: Adaptation stream equals evaluation stream (reported accuracy over a single pass with earlier items' labelled reflections feeding later ones; batch 1 is cold start); correctness tags enter memory despite the 'no ground-truth' framing; the experience curve reuses the same problems over passes; cross-task transfer is only preliminary and mixed; no contamination or split analysis.

E.statistics.reason: Main table uses three seeds with 95% CIs and token SDs; order-shuffle check; Spearman test for first-try quality. But several top cells overlap with the best baseline (Qwen3-8B MATH-500, Llama Game-of-24), Game-of-24 has only 100 problems, and ablation/iteration/transfer tables are single runs without intervals.

E.cost.reason: Decoding tokens per instance are reported for all methods against heavier test-time scaling baselines, plus an iteration-budget study. Not clear that distillation, consolidation and per-role prompt-composer calls are counted; no accuracy-at-matched-compute comparison against label-using memory baselines; overhead acknowledged as a limitation.
